newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares soar 6.45 pct to new record.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares soar 6.45 pct to new record.

text.p: Istanbul shares soared in strong activity on Friday amid growing hopes that a secularist coalition planned by conservative leader Mesut Yilmaz could win a vote of confidence in parliament, brokers said.

The IMKB National-100 closed at an all-time high of 1,815, up 110 points, or 6.45 percent from Thursday and compared to a previous record of 1,774 on Monday, June 23. Weekly gains totalled 10.5 percent after last week's 3.7 percent rise.
Volume more than doubled to 49.52 trillion lira ($335.9 million) from Thursday's 19.33 trillion ($131.5 million).

"The market posted further gains with every deputy resignation from the pro-Islamist alliance today. The expectation is that the coalition to be formed by Yilmaz will win a confidence vote in parliament," Cumali Ekinci from Aks securities.
Brokers expect the market to target the index's 1,850 level early next week if positive expectations continue.
Three deputies from the ruling Islamist-led coalition's junior partner True Path Party (DYP) and one from the Islamist Welfare Party quit their parties this morning.
Yilmaz has said he would present his cabinet list to President Suleyman Demirel early next week.
He has won the support of two left-wing parties, a small right-wing grouping and conservative independent MPs.

With the latest resignations, the number of MPs expected to back Yilmaz rose to 272 in the 550-seat parliament, compared with 275 deputies supporting the Islamists and their allies. Two seats are vacant and the speaker has no vote.
DYP leader Tansu Ciller has refused to discuss rival Yilmaz's offer to join the secularist pact.
